# Bonsai Studio
Open dist/index.html in a modern browser. Choose a seed and branching density, grow the tree, then download a PNG. The same settings reproduce the same tree.
## Upstream and changes
John Allbritten’s cbonsai generates configurable bonsai in a C and ncurses terminal. Its upstream README covers package installation, source builds, and static or animated growth. See UPSTREAM-README.md or https://gitlab.com/jallbrit/cbonsai.
Bonsai Studio adapts the movement distributions in cbonsai.c for trunks, left and right shoots, and foliage. Browser rendering uses Canvas, a seeded generator and a bounded branch model. Seeds are specific to this edition. The adapted source is in dist/index.html and is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE.
# JOGENERATEqa — Repository Studio

## Page 1 — Purpose and upstream

JOGENERATEqa turns the saved JOGENERATE shortlist into a browser workspace. It preserves the 40 reviewed repository records, divided evenly across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and SourceForge. The selected result is Bonsai Studio, a browser adaptation of John Allbritten’s cbonsai. The studio lets you review the evidence behind the choice and run the selected application without cloning or executing every project in the shortlist.

The upstream cbonsai README describes a C and ncurses bonsai generator, installation through package managers or source builds, and static versus live growth. The complete upstream README travels with the selected project. This guide extends it with browser instructions, the studio’s QA workflow and the handoff format. The terminal original remains available at https://gitlab.com/jallbrit/cbonsai. Use it for its documented CLI options and native installation procedures.

Bonsai Studio expresses the branching idea through a Canvas implementation. Choose a seed, control density and grow the tree. A seed reproduces a tree in this port when the other settings are unchanged. It need not match a tree generated by the terminal version. The port's adapted source and GPL notice remain in the download.

## Page 2 — Evidence and shortlist

The initial list is the archived selection made at 12:06:43 GMT on 13 November 2026. It is a reproducible starting point, not a live claim about the latest repositories today. The original selection sampled 60 results per platform and shortlisted ten from each based on originality, practical value and inspectable code or documentation. The original shortlist is retained in the bundle.

GitHub used indexed public results sorted by creation and can lag. GitLab used its public project feed; temporary scan copies were mapped to their originals where known. Bitbucket used Atlassian’s public workspace because its global endpoint was unavailable. SourceForge used the directory’s Last Updated order, which is not creation order and includes mirrors. Rank and feed position are different fields: the former is the shortlist ranking, the latter is the position in the original sample.

Descriptions are examples of what to explore, not claims that every project was installed or tested. Fork, mirror and scan-copy labels document known provenance. Verify licence, maintenance and suitability at the original before making a release decision.

## Page 3 — Reviewing and editing

Open Repositories to see 40 records in a scrollable window. Search project names, descriptions and notes or narrow the list by platform. Click a name to open a second window with the repository’s description and original link. Edit opens a form for project name, URL, provenance label, description and notes. Platform, rank and original feed position remain fixed so the selection stays auditable.

Save record stores edits in this browser. If browser storage is unavailable, the edits remain available for the current session and can still be exported. A URL must use HTTPS and match the repository’s platform. The list maintains the original count; changing notes or a URL does not change which application was built.

Pin keeps a window open when Escape is pressed. Close explicitly dismisses a pinned or unpinned window. The topmost unpinned window is the one Escape closes. Windows scroll independently and can be resized where the browser supports it. The surrounding page scrolls between a fixed header and footer.

## Page 4 — Rendering and fallback

Render & preview opens Bonsai Studio in a sandboxed browser frame. No package installation or native binary is needed. The selected GitLab record also offers this render action. The preview runs the saved port, not a remote build. This keeps the result reproducible and prevents unknown repository scripts or installation steps from running in the studio.

For other records, Try embedded repository requests a framed view of the original host. Some hosts forbid this with framing policies. If the frame is blank or blocked, use Open original to inspect the repository in another tab. The original link is visible before attempting the embed; the browser does not reliably expose a cross-origin framing failure for automatic detection. Internet access is required for external repository pages and the Contact form.

English is the default interface language. Select Arabic, French or Spanish in the header; Arabic applies right-to-left layout. Source descriptions and Markdown documents retain their original language. Use the selected application's own language controls inside its preview. Header and footer documentation controls open the same gold-accented panels. Contact opens the external form in a panel with an original link.

## Page 5 — Download, provenance and QA

Download project ZIP creates JO_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.zip using Europe/London time. The archive contains the complete selected browser application, its adapted source, upstream README and licence, operating documents, PDF guide and the initial shortlist. SHORTLIST-EDITED.json carries your current 40 records. PROJECT.json identifies the archive, original repository, selection snapshot and launch file. The archived initial selection is separate from your editable snapshot.

Extract the ZIP and open its dist/index.html. The ZIP packages Bonsai Studio, not 40 native repositories. The separate JOGENERATEqa distribution includes the review studio and bundled port. The app does not require an API key or build server; a static host is suitable. Record edits are local to the current browser and origin and are not sent to the repo hosts.

For a handoff, check the selected source in PROJECT.json, inspect your notes, and run the extracted entry point. Use TESTS.md for verification evidence. Keep the licence and upstream attribution with the adapted code. The documentation describes the saved snapshot and its limitations so future reviewers can distinguish original evidence from subsequent edits.
